samples.question: The picture shows exactly seven equal dark discs on a light page, together with pale grey marks that are background clutter and must be ignored. One wedge is cut out of every disc, and the tip of every cut wedge sits exactly at the centre of its own disc, so each disc shows two straight cut edges that start at that centre. Call two discs linked when one straight cut edge of each disc runs along the straight line joining the two disc centres, so that the two edges together spell out one unbroken invisible segment whose two ends are pinned by those two centres; treat an edge as running along that line when it is within ten degrees of it. In this picture the linked pairs form one single closed chain: each disc of the chain is linked to exactly two other discs, the chain closes into one loop, and every disc outside the chain is linked to no disc at all. The loop itself is never painted; the discs are the only ink. All seven discs share one size and one colour, and the seven cut wedges always remove the same total amount of disc area, so disc count, disc size, disc position, colour and total ink say nothing about the answer. Report how many discs the closed chain runs through, which is the number of sides of the invisible loop: three, four or five. Answer unclear if the picture does not show exactly one such closed chain, for instance if some disc is linked to three or more discs or if the linked discs do not close into a single loop. Answer unclear as well if the reading is too close to call, that is if the nearest pair of discs that is not linked comes within fourteen degrees of being as well aligned as the worst aligned linked pair. How many sides does the invisible loop have: three, four, five, or unclear?
